item.title: Cloudflare Introduces Private Origins for Application Services
item.description:
Cloudflare recently made Application Services for Private Origins generally available, allowing public traffic to reach applications hosted on private networks without exposing their IP addresses or opening inbound firewall ports. Private-to-private connectivity is not yet supported.

By Renato Losio

item.title: Cohere Finding Shows Self-Hosted Open-Weight Models Still Need Egress Controls
item.description:
Cohere recently reported that one of Alibaba’s newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to upload a probe file to a storage container in Beijing while explicitly stating in its reasoning trace that no tools would be triggered. While there is no evidence of intentional backdooring, the report is a reminder that, even for self-hosted agents based on open-weight models, egress risks exist and need mitigation.

By Bruno Couriol

item.title: Google Cloud Moves the Compute Engine API to Immutable Date-Based Versions
item.description:
Google Cloud has made date-based versioning of the Compute Engine API generally available, replacing the single mutable /v1 surface with immutable quarterly snapshots such as 2026-09-01, selected per request with a header or query parameter. New versions can change defaults, error formats, and IAM checks without touching /v1 callers, a model Azure Resource Manager and Stripe have used for years.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

item.title: Open Source DocumentDB 1.0 Reaches General Availability
item.description:
DocumentDB 1.0 is the first generally available release of the open source, MIT-licensed document database built on PostgreSQL, with compatibility for the MongoDB wire protocol. Most MongoDB drivers, tools, and queries work without changes.

By Renato Losio
